lessons.title: Industries, power and where factories are located

objectives: Classify economic activities as primary, secondary and tertiary
Explain the factors for locating industries
Describe sources of energy and hydroelectric power
reviewNotes: Teacher to verify industrial examples (aluminium at Edéa, refinery at Limbe, cement, sugar, textiles) and hydroelectric sites (Edéa, Song-Loulou on the Sanaga, Lagdo on the Benue); their current status should be checked.

Draft for teacher review: this course follows the Cameroon anglophone secondary Geography syllabus as generally understood; scope and level per Form, places, figures and examples must be checked against the official syllabus and a current atlas before release.

blocks.md: Economic activities are grouped in three levels. **Primary** activities take raw materials from nature (farming, fishing, logging, mining). **Secondary** activities turn them into finished goods (manufacturing, food processing, construction). **Tertiary** activities provide services (trade, transport, banking, teaching, health). **Industry** is mainly the secondary sector, where raw materials gain value.

blocks.caption: From water to electricity
blocks.alt: Four boxes showing the steps of hydroelectric power.

blocks.title: Factors of industrial location
blocks.md: A factory is placed where costs are low and sales are high: near **raw materials**, **power** (electricity, fuel), **water**, a **market** of buyers, **labour**, **transport** (roads, railway, port), **capital** and a **government** policy that allows it. Industries using heavy raw materials locate near them; others locate close to markets.

blocks.title: Industries and power in Cameroon
blocks.md: Examples: food and drink processing (sugar, beer, flour, palm oil, cocoa), **timber** and wood products, **cement**, **aluminium** smelting at Edéa, **oil refining** at Limbe, textiles and cotton ginning in the north. Electricity comes mostly from **hydroelectric power** on the Sanaga (Edéa, Song-Loulou) and the Benue (Lagdo), and also from thermal (oil or gas) plants and growing solar projects.

**Hydroelectric power (HEP)** uses falling water: a dam stores water in a reservoir, the water runs through pipes to turn **turbines**, and the turbines drive **generators** that produce electricity. HEP needs a river with a good flow and a drop, and is clean and cheap to run but costly to build; dams may flood land and need resettlement. Other energy: **fuelwood**, **petroleum**, **gas**, **solar** and **wind**.

blocks.title: Be careful
blocks.md:
- Primary activities give raw materials; they do not make finished goods.
- Cheap power alone does not decide location: you also need market, labour and transport.
- Renewable energy (water, sun, wind) is not used up; fuelwood is renewable only if trees are replanted.

blocks.title: Example 1: classify
blocks.statement: Classify these as primary, secondary or tertiary: cocoa farming, chocolate making, selling chocolate.
steps: Growing cocoa takes from nature: primary.

blocks.title: Example 2: location
blocks.statement: Why might a cement factory be built close to limestone deposits?
steps: Limestone is heavy and bulky to carry.
Carrying it far would raise costs.
So a site near the raw material saves transport costs.
blocks.answer: To reduce the transport cost of heavy raw materials.
